content:
For a fixed \(k\)-element subset of the six values, exactly \(\frac{6!}{k!}\) permutations put those \(k\) values in increasing order. There are \(\binom{6}{k}\) such subsets, so the total number of length-\(k\) increasing subsequences over all permutations is

\[
\binom{6}{k}\frac{6!}{k!}.
\]

Thus

\[
\sum_{\pi} S(\pi)
=
\sum_{k=2}^{6} \binom{6}{k}\frac{6!}{k!}.
\]

Compute:

\[
\begin{aligned}
k=2 &: \binom{6}{2}\frac{720}{2}=15\cdot 360=5400,\\
k=3 &: \binom{6}{3}\frac{720}{6}=20\cdot 120=2400,\\
k=4 &: \binom{6}{4}\frac{720}{24}=15\cdot 30=450,\\
k=5 &: \binom{6}{5}\frac{720}{120}=6\cdot 6=36,\\
k=6 &: \binom{6}{6}\frac{720}{720}=1.
\end{aligned}
\]

Summing:

\[
5400+2400+450+36+1=8287.
\]

\[
\boxed{8287}
\]
